req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-030 requires DELETE /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} to be idempotent: the first call returns HTTP 204, and every subsequent call for the same squad number returns HTTP 404. The test suite covers: (1) positive/STC — the full state transition from 'player exists' → first DELETE (204) → second DELETE (404); (2) negative/NEG — DELETE on a squad number that never existed returns 404 immediately; (3) boundary/BVA — the exact transition point between the first and second call, asserting the status codes are exactly 204 and 404 (not 200, not 400, not 500), catching operator-flip and constant-bump mutations; (4) DT — a third consecutive DELETE still returns 404, confirming idempotency holds beyond the second call; (5) EP — verifying a different existing player can still be deleted independently, confirming the idempotency is scoped per squad number. All tests use the pre-loaded fixture data and the in-process FastAPI TestClient.

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_first_204_second_404
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 (Messi) exists in the database
FastAPI app is loaded in-process via TestClient
expected: First DELETE returns HTTP 204 No Content
Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 Not Found
State transition: exists -> deleted -> not-found is correct
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_first_204_second_404():
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
    assert r2.status_code == 404

tests.name: test_delete_boundary_exact_transition_204_then_404
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=1 (Armani) exists in the database
FastAPI app is loaded in-process via TestClient
actions: Send DELETE /players/squadnumber/1 again — assert exactly 404 (not 204, not 500)
trace: R-PLAYER-030: boundary at the exact call-count transition point
BVA: boundary between call-1 (204) and call-2 (404)
Catches off-by-one mutations on status constants and condition flips
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_boundary_exact_transition_204_then_404():
    get_before = client.get('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert get_before.status_code == 200
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    assert r1.status_code != 200
    assert r1.status_code != 404
    get_after = client.get('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert get_after.status_code == 404
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    assert r2.status_code != 204
    assert r2.status_code != 500

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_scoped_per_squad_number
preconditions: Players with squadNumber=7 (de Paul) and squadNumber=11 (Di Maria) exist
FastAPI app is loaded in-process via TestClient
expected: Idempotency is scoped per squad number, not global
Deleting squad 11 twice independently yields 204 then 404
trace: R-PLAYER-030: idempotency applies per playerId independently
EP: equivalence partition — each squad number is an independent resource
Catches mutations that share state across resources or use wrong key
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_idempotent_scoped_per_squad_number():
    r7a = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/7')
    assert r7a.status_code == 204
    r7b = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/7')
    assert r7b.status_code == 404
    r11a = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/11')
    assert r11a.status_code == 204
    r11b = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/11')
    assert r11b.status_code == 404
